statement: Lena had some stickers. She gave half of them to her brother, then gave 4 to a friend, and then bought 10 more. She now has 30 stickers. How many stickers did she have at the start?

choices.misconception: I undid the steps but in the original order: I doubled first, then added 4, then took away 10.
I undid the purchase and the gift to the friend but forgot to undo the halving.
I applied her steps forwards to the 30 instead of undoing them.
I undid the gift to the friend by taking away 4 instead of adding the 4 back.

hints: Start from the 30 and walk through the story in reverse.
Work backwards: undo the last step first, and undo each step with its opposite operation. Buying becomes giving back, giving away becomes getting back, and halving becomes doubling.
Before buying 10 she had 20. Before giving 4 away she had 24. Those 24 are the half she kept.

solutions.reliable: Undo the steps from last to first. Before buying 10 she had 30 - 10 = 20. Before giving 4 away she had 20 + 4 = 24. Those 24 were the half she kept, so she started with 2 x 24 = 48. Check forwards: 48, then 24, then 20, then 30. The transferable idea: to work backwards, reverse both the order of the steps and each operation.

whyOnTest: Working backwards needs the steps reversed in order and in operation, and each half-reversed attempt gives one of the other choices.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
